chunks: Verily, when Allah, Blessed and High, took the covenants of the servants, He commanded the (Black) Stone, so it swallowed them. And for that reason, (the pilgrim) says: 'My entrustment, I have fulfilled it, and my covenant I have renewed, so that you (the Stone) may testify for me with loyalty.'

key_terms.الْحَجَر: the Black Stone (Hajjar al-Aswad) — the sacred stone in the Ka'ba at Mecca
key_terms.الْعِبَاد: servants/worshippers — all of humanity in their pre-existential state before creation
key_terms.الْمُوَافَاة: loyalty/fulfillment — the quality of remaining true to one's covenant
key_terms.مَوَاثِيق: covenants/pledges (plural of mithaq) — the primordial agreements between Allah and souls before creation

ai.seo_question: Why do pilgrims speak to the Black Stone during Hajj according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) explains the spiritual significance of the Black Stone (Hajjar al-Aswad) in Mecca: it was commanded by Allah to swallow the primordial covenants taken from all souls before creation. The supplication recited when kissing or touching the Black Stone during Hajj acknowledges this pre-eternal covenant, asking the Stone to bear witness on the Day of Judgment that the believer remained loyal to their covenant with Allah. This hadith contextualizes the Hajj ritual within the broader theology of the primordial covenant (mithaq), connecting the physical act of touching the Stone to the soul's primordial testimony before Allah.
